newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turkish forces detain four Germans on Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Turkish forces detain four Germans on Cyprus.

text.p: Turkish forces detained four German tourists on Monday for straying across a ceasefire line guarded by soldiers into Turkish-occupied northern Cyprus, diplomats on the island said.

A German diplomat said the tourists, three men and a woman, were detained by Turkish forces in the south east Famagusta area at around 11.00 a.m. (0900 GMT), just off the boundary of the British military base of Dhekelia.

"We are aware of the case and are trying to help these people," a duty officer at the German Embassy in Nicosia told Reuters, adding he was still trying to confirm police reports that they were actually German.
"We don't know the details...we are trying to get them free," he added.
A British High Commission spokesman quoting preliminary Cyprus police reports said the tourists had walked north of the ceasefire line skirting the boundary when they were detained.
A retired fireman was shot dead by Turkish forces in the same area in October when he entered Turkish-held territory. His relatives said he had been collecting snails at the time.
The killing was one of a series of ceasefire line incidents classed by the United Nations as the most violent since Turkish troops invaded the island 22 years ago.
Turkey invaded northern Cyprus in 1974 in the wake of a brief Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military ruling in Greece at the time. Some 30,000 mainland Turkish troops are stationed on Cyprus.
